Colour lookup tables (colormaps)

Source: R/lut.R
lut.Rd

Creates a lookup table (LUT) that colours a channel with a colormap such as magma or viridis instead of a single colour. Use it in adjust_colors() or as the colour of add_overlay(). Intensities at or below the lower end of the display range (see adjust_exposure()) get the first colour of the map, at or above the upper end its last colour.

Usage

lut(colors, reverse = FALSE)

Arguments

colors

The name of a colormap, or a vector of two or more colours. Colormaps are the perceptually uniform maps of the viridisLite package: "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "viridis", "cividis", "rocket", "mako" and "turbo". Colours are spread evenly from the lower to the upper end of the display range, for example c("black", "red", "yellow").

reverse

If TRUE, the map runs the other way round.

Value

A tidymontage_lut object.

Details

Colormaps work best for single-channel panels with quantitative content, such as calcium imaging, ratio images or intensity heatmaps: perceptually uniform maps like magma and viridis show differences in intensity more faithfully than a single colour does.

Merges need single colours, since colours add up like light. In a merge, a channel coloured with a LUT uses its original colour from the image metadata (the color column) instead, unless add_merge() sets one. In its own panels, a LUT channel is drawn on the first colour of its map, and add_color_legend() shows it as a colour bar.

Examples

lut("magma")
#> <tidymontage_lut> lut("magma")
lut("viridis", reverse = TRUE)
#> <tidymontage_lut> lut("viridis", reverse = TRUE)
lut(c("black", "darkred", "orange", "white"))
#> <tidymontage_lut> lut(c("black", "darkred", "orange", "white"))

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
montage |> adjust_colors(GCaMP = lut("magma"))
} # }
